intro.text: A Beaconite on Canticle who takes Rebeke's radio call as she returns from a raid on the Cinder King's city and grants her access to Beacon.

A citizen of Beacon on Canticle and its field commander and special operations planner under the Greater Good. He plans and leads the raids on Union, taking part with his team in the most difficult parts of each mission.

items.text: Zeal was once a citizen of Union but broke away with the other Beaconites. He ran special operations for their Lodestar, Elegy, and for the Greater Good.

Zeal led a raid on Union to rescue captured Beaconites, using a device to hack the Charred's bracers and disable them all at once. While the raiders bombed the arena, he and his team slipped onto the Cinder King's private ship and stole the Scadrian authorization key, which they believed opened the Refuge of Stone, leaving a fake in its place.

On the way home, Rebeke radioed for signal alignment. Relieved to hear her, Zeal asked after her brother and offered condolences on his death. He angrily rebuked her for taking Elegy against the Greater Good's orders but let her in. Hearing of the stranger with her, he first asked whether he was dangerous.

Meeting Rebeke at Beacon, Zeal asked Nomad's name and, hearing only Alethi, tried sign language in case he was deaf. He sent the injured Thomos for treatment and failed to stir Elegy's memory. He took custody of Nomad for the meeting with the Greater Good, keeping a hand on the device that could activate Nomad's bracers.

Zeal told the Greater Good that Thomos had muttered about Nomad touching the sun and living, and offered Nomad's strange speech as further evidence that he might be one of the Sunlit Ones. He produced the stolen key and argued it was genuine, and the council commended him and his team.

When Nomad offered to help open the door to the Refuge, Zeal urged the Greater Good to accept, relishing the irony of finding safety behind the door the Cinder King had long sought, and wondering if Adonalsium had sent Nomad. After a failed lie that he lacked the keys, he removed Nomad's bracers on the council's orders, watching him closely.

Driven into the southern corridor, Beacon's leaders met again. Zeal flatly rejected surrender, saying he would rather die than become another source of the Cinder King's power. He reported the paths north blockaded and explained that he had scouted the mountains for Elegy and found no way through.
When Confidence despaired that the Refuge might be a myth, Zeal countered that they were nothing without hope, and he would rather hope a myth was true than give up and be consumed by the sun.

With Rebeke, Zeal brought Nomad to the Reliquary so the Chorus could manufacture parts for his engines. He explained that the shades would kill anyone who entered, and that he wasn't sure whether they were self-aware. When Rebeke thought she saw her brother among them, he gently pointed out that she couldn't know for certain.

Zeal had the Chorus build Nomad's parts from his schematics, explaining that Beacon had stolen some of Union's smoke and an older containment unit when it broke away. While they waited, he fetched snacks, puzzled by Nomad's request for something spicy.
Zeal watched the test of Nomad's prototype engine and saw to the Greater Good's needs as they prepared to fly over the mountain.

Summoned by Nomad, Zeal used his device to knock Elegy out so she could be restrained again, and was incredulous to hear she had spoken. He asked about the guns in Nomad's notes, but signal horns interrupted them as Beacon began jettisoning ships to save power.

After the crash beyond the mountain, Zeal reported about two and a half hours before the sun would cut off escape, and offered to lead his team to steal more sunhearts. He begged a doubtful Confidence to let him try, and readily agreed to Nomad's plan to dig up new sunhearts in the great maelstrom.

Zeal gathered his team and left on the Dawnchaser within ten minutes, briefing them while standing on a chair and joking that they would do the digging while he ran things from the cab. Inside the burning maelstrom, he could only watch the temperature climb until Nomad heard the sunhearts and went out.

When Rebeke collapsed from the heat, Zeal took the controls and flew back into darkness. Believing Nomad dead, he resolved to steal sunhearts from the Cinder King's forces alone, praying to Adonalsium as he crept up and picked the vault lock, only to find Nomad already inside. As they fled, the Cinder King followed.

Pursued by Charred, Zeal reached the Dawnchaser and barricaded the door with Rebeke while Nomad fought on the deck, then took off at his signal. Once clear of the radio jammer, he reported to Confidence that they had five sunhearts and were on their way.

Zeal piloted one of Beacon's new gunships, armed with a sunheart-powered cannon, escorting the transports through the Cinder King's forces. When Charred boarded his ship, Zellion and Elegy leapt aboard and killed them. At the Refuge's entrance, he handed Zellion the authorization key, which Zellion returned as unneeded.
As the Beaconites tried to flee one last time, Zellion saw a gunship, possibly Zeal's, go down.

appearance.text: A little person standing under four feet tall, with dark brown eyes, shorter-than-average arms and legs and a typically sized head.

personality.text: Formal with his superiors but relaxed and jovial with his team, joking and laughing with them even in dire situations. He leaves most fieldwork to them and organizes the operations.

Extraordinarily stalwart, he repeatedly puts duty to his people above his own life, and he thinks outside the box more than most Beaconites. He follows Adonalsium, believing it plays an active, conscious role in the cosmere.
